title: Saint Oren's Shade
summary: The group reaches Saint Oren's, a settled community built directly around a massive exposed structure most travelers would call a Sunforge. Nobody assigns Kael another identity.

panelPlan.text: The settlement wraps naturally around a huge black ribbed structure used for shade, tables and a children's climbing boundary. No one treats it as sacred or technical.
Mira Sloan welcomes the travelers, asks their actual names and writes them on a meal board.
Eva watches Kael's name remain Kael through an entire introduction.

directionInline.text: The obvious Sunforge proximity should be visually undeniable while socially unremarkable.

title: Samuel Stays
summary: Samuel learns that Pell Oren, an elderly community member, is dying and has been asking for someone willing to sit with his estranged daughter. Samuel asks the group to stay a few days.

panelPlan.text: Pell lies in a bright back room with family moving normally around him rather than posing in vigil.
Mira tells Samuel that Pell's daughter refuses to enter because their last conversation ended badly.
Samuel asks Jessa whether the group can remain. It is the first time his pastoral obligation, not Veyra's investigation, determines the route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Pell Oren is dying. His daughter won't come inside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: And you think you can fix that?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: You finally asked before deciding for us.

directionInline.text: Samuel's care now has priority over his old role as advance manipulator. Do not make the death a clue delivery mechanism.

title: Day Two
summary: A second uneventful day makes Eva restless and Veyra methodical. Kael becomes legible through ordinary behavior: he loses at cards, helps Pell outside, and knows exactly as much about the mystery as he claimed.

panelPlan.text: Montage-like sequential page: Kael loses coins at a card table and looks genuinely annoyed; later he helps Pell sit under the black Sunforge rib.
Eva notes every absence of recognition while Veyra checks old guest books for similar faces or names.
Jessa catches Eva watching Kael laugh at a bad joke and asks what theory that supports.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I thought he'd be good at cards.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Nobody here has mistaken him for anybody.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Nobody here has had time. They're busy beating him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: So am I. You're waiting for him to become evidence and missing the part where he's a terrible loser.

directionInline.text: This page is important character development. Kael becomes knowable through ordinary time rather than exposition.

title: Veyra's Empty Page
summary: Veyra cannot make Saint Oren's fit her emerging correlation. The largest and most obvious Sunforge-like structure they have encountered produces no identity event, no unusual arrival and no Cadre convergence.

panelPlan.text: Veyra sits beneath the black structure with maps and notes spread around her, drawing lines and then crossing them out.
Eva offers increasingly broad theories. Jessa asks whether Veyra may have grouped unlike things under one name.
Kael passes with a tray of food, listens to three sentences and declines to join.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: If the structure matters, this should be the loudest place we've seen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: The people here don't even use these things the same way.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Fine. But that still gives you three objects and one word.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What would convince you they aren't the same thing?

directionInline.text: Attack the category without resolving it. Veyra is allowed to be intelligent and still discover that her taxonomy may be wrong.

title: Pell's Last Evening
summary: Samuel helps Pell and his daughter speak before Pell dies. The issue's emotional center belongs entirely to people whose lives have nothing to do with Kael's mystery.

panelPlan.text: Samuel sits between Pell and his daughter only long enough to get them speaking directly to each other, then moves his chair back.
Kael, Eva and Jessa remain outside with Mira, giving the family privacy and talking quietly about ordinary things.
Later, Samuel emerges and says Pell died after midnight. Nobody asks whether the Sunforge had anything to do with it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: They finally said what they were angry about.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: A little. It was what there was time for.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Sometimes that's enough for one night.

directionInline.text: Samuel's pastoral identity must become valuable independently of the mystery. No hidden clue is delivered by the dying man.

title: Four Quiet Days
summary: After four quiet days, the group leaves Saint Oren's with no anomalous event to explain. The negative case matters: an obvious Sunforge and Kael can coexist without the pattern appearing.

panelPlan.text: The group says goodbye after Pell's simple burial. Mira calls each traveler by the correct name.
Eva looks back at the enormous black structure and closes her notebook rather than adding another theory.
On the road, Jessa lists ordinary things they learned about Kael. Kael objects only when she gets to his card playing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I know. I didn't like it.

directionInline.text: Close on the distinction between a life being eventful and the mystery being active. This is another falsifier, not filler.
